title: OpsCat Portfolio Demo Narrative & Operator Walkthrough
portfolio_pitch: OpsCat is a local/mock agentic AI incident-response/operator-replacement evidence system. It shows how an operator loop can observe, correlate, investigate, decide, draft safe actions, verify outcomes, report evidence, and improve from gaps without claiming production autonomy.

target_role_signals.portfolio_readout: Uses provider-shaped readers, correlation, runbook, policy, verification, reporting, and evidence-pack tools with structured inputs and outputs.
Every decision is tied to evidence references, acceptance stages, proof points, and reportable output rather than free-form claims.
Risk, approval, side-effect, and forbidden-claim gates are modeled before any action-like path is considered.
The local/mock loop demonstrates observe-to-report progression and safe auto-run readiness without production execution.
Acceptance drills, release evidence, eval profiles, and docs gates make the portfolio claims reproducible.
High-risk, low-confidence, protected, or human-gated scenarios remain explicit handoffs instead of silent automation.
The demo proves local/mock operator-replacement mechanics only: zero executions, zero live calls, zero credentials, zero network, and no production mutation.

architecture_sections.summary: FastAPI and service-layer state model incidents, evidence, approvals, policies, reports, and audit artifacts.
Provider-shaped local/mock tools collect context, normalize signals, select runbooks, and prepare safe drafts.
The operator loop progresses from observation to correlation, investigation, decision, safe draft/action boundary, verification, reporting, and improvement.
Policy, risk, approval, evidence sufficiency, readiness, and side-effect counters keep automation inside the local/mock dry-run boundary.
Acceptance drills, release evidence, roadmap summaries, and docs-profile tests make portfolio claims auditable.

operator_walkthrough_steps.operator_view: OpsCat starts from provider-shaped alert or fixture evidence and captures service, severity, environment, and timeline state.
Signals are grouped with deployment, metric, and incident context so the operator can see likely relationships.
Read-only local/mock context tools produce evidence-grounded hypotheses and candidate causes.
Readiness, confidence, policy, and evidence gates decide whether to proceed, hand off, or block.
OpsCat prepares report, ticket, rollback, or remediation drafts as metadata, not uncontrolled production mutation.
The P93 pack records zero executions and only points to local/mock dry-run evidence; live or production execution remains forbidden.
Post-action and acceptance evidence prove whether a local/mock path is demo-ready, shadow-only, human-gated, or blocked.
Generated Markdown and release docs make the incident and portfolio evidence easy to inspect.
Remaining gaps are kept in roadmap and release evidence so the portfolio does not overstate production maturity.

proof_points: P92 acceptance drill proves six local/mock operator-replacement scenarios with executions=0.
P90 and P91 separate readiness decisions from remediation-gap planning.
Policy and approval gates remain visible instead of hidden behind a chatbot answer.
Docs-profile verification checks release evidence, roadmap, README, and demo narrative wiring.
The CLI smoke emits count-style evidence for walkthrough steps, proof points, commands, and zero executions.
Forbidden claims explicitly block production autonomy, live API operation, credentialed operation, and production remediation claims.
The README now places the portfolio story, local/mock boundary, quick demo command, and evidence links near the top.

demo_commands.purpose: Runs the complete local gate when a reviewer wants the full release proof.

remaining_gaps: Production auth and tenant administration remain out of scope.
Live connector OAuth, real provider mutation, and secret-manager integration remain out of scope.
Hosted workers, queue HA, load/soak testing, production deployment, backup/restore, and self-monitoring remain future work.
Production operator replacement requires supervised shadow evidence, human approval workflows, security review, and explicit owner approval.
